speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Health)
text: They may try to contact family members or visit them at their last known addresses to encourage them to visit their loved ones.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Many nursing homes are also run by voluntary welfare organisations and may tap on charitable donations to provide further financial support to their residents.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Have there been any cases that the Ministry is aware of where because of the inability to pay, the resident of the nursing home could not continue to reside in the nursing home?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Second, is there a procedure for what nursing homes should do in case they decide that the bill is not being paid and they cannot afford to keep the resident there?

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Like I have mentioned, nursing homes do have certain procedures to try to establish contact with the family members of the residents.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Different nursing homes have different procedures but, fundamentally, they are quite similar.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: They will make phone calls, they will try to email them, they can send letters, and some will also attempt to visit their homes at the last known address.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: While the Government can provide financial support through the various assistance schemes that I have mentioned just now, we cannot play surrogacy to the love and warmth of the family.
